{{Short description|Swiss biochemist (1951–2011)}}
'''Jürg Tschopp''' (born 1951 in [[Basel]] — died 22 March 2011 in the [[Swiss Alps]]) was a Swiss biochemist, known for his research on [[apoptosis]] and the immunology of inflammation.<ref>{{cite journal|author=O'Neill, Luke A.|title=Jürg Tschopp (1951–2011)|journal=Science|volume=332|issue=6030|year=2011|page=679|doi=10.1126/science.1207046|pmid=21551056|bibcode=2011Sci...332..679O|s2cid=34300772}}</ref> His greatest achievement was perhaps his team's discovery and scientific description of the [[inflammasome]] (which he named).<ref name=NatureImmunology>{{cite journal|doi=10.1038/ni0511-367|title=Jürg Tschopp 1951–2011|year=2011|last1=Budd|first1=Ralph C.|last2=Schneider|first2=Pascal|last3=MacKay|first3=Fabienne|last4=Strasser|first4=Andreas|journal=Nature Immunology|volume=12|issue=5|page=367|s2cid=21458106|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Biography==
Tschopp studied [[chemistry]] with his 1974 ''Diplom'' thesis supervised by [[Joachim Seelig]] at the [[Biozentrum University of Basel]]. There Tschopp received in 1979 his doctorate in [[biophysics]] under the supervision of Jürgen Engel.<ref name=EJI>{{cite journal|doi=10.1002/eji.201190025|author=Romero, Pedro|title=Professor Jürg Tschopp (1951-2011)|journal=European Journal of Immunology|year=2011|volume=41|issue=5|pages=1189–1190|pmid=21523778}}</ref> As a postdoc Tschopp was supervised by [[Hans J. Müller-Eberhard]] at the [[Scripps Research|Scripps Research Institute]] in [[La Jolla]]. There with colleagues he showed "that the [[Complement membrane attack complex|lytic pore of complement]] was formed by [[Complement component 9|C9]] [[multimer]]s."<ref name=CellJournal>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/j.cell.2011.04.027|title=Jürg Tschopp 1951–2011|year=2011|last1=Flavell|first1=Richard A.|journal=Cell|volume=145|issue=4|pages=493–494|s2cid=1156521|doi-access=free}}</ref> At the [[University of Lausanne]], Tschopp became an assistant professor in 1982, an associate professor in 1987, and a full professor in 1990 in the biochemistry department. Since 2003 he was a co-director of the biochemistry department.<ref name=EJI/>

He and his colleagues discovered "viral and mammalian forms of the [[Caspase 8|caspase-8]]-related protein [[CFLAR|FLIP]]" (FLICE-Like Inhibitory Protein, where "FLICE" is an alias for caspase-8). They elucidated the molecular mechanisms of caspase-8's involvement in cell death processes and in nonapoptotic signalling pathways.<ref name=NatureImmunology/> In 2000 he with 9 co-workers published their discovery "that, similar to apoptosis, caspase-independent cell death ([[necroptosis]]) was a tightly controlled cell biological process that was dependent on the [[kinase]] [[Ribosome-inactivating protein|RIP1]]."<ref name=EJI/>

He was involved in the discovery of [[B-cell activating factor]] (BAFF), also known as B Lymphocyte Stimulator (BLyS), a cytokine that stimulates the reproduction of B cells. This led to the development of a new drug, [[Belimumab]], approved by the [[Food and Drug Administration|FDA]] in 2011 for [[systemic lupus erythematosus]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Dixit, Vishva|title=Jürg Tschopp (1951–2011). Immunologist whose discoveries transformed patients' lives|journal=Nature|volume=472|year=2011|issue=7343|page=296|doi=10.1038/472296a|pmid=21512562|s2cid=205063864|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Tschopp's group, and other groups, established that mutations in the gene for the protein [[NLRP3|NLRP3, also known as cryopyrin]], (one of the proteins forming the [[inflammasome]]) cause [[cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome]] (CAPS), which is a group of rare autoimmune disorders. Patients with CAPS are "now successfully treated with IL-1 antagonists such as [[anakinra]] or blocking antibodies."<ref name=EJI/>

In 2005, Tschopp with six colleagues described the function of a "novel cytoplasmic protein complex" involving [[Mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein|what is now known as Mitochondrial Antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS), also known as CARDIF or Cardif]].<ref name=EJI/>

He died of a heart attack on a ski trip with his son in the Swiss Alps.<ref name=EJI/> In his youth he was nationally ranked in the [[decathlon]] and was later active in hiking, running, and skiing.<ref name=NatureImmunology/>

When Tschopp died he had an [[h-index]] of 105.<ref name=CDD>{{cite journal|author=Kroemer, G.|author2=Martinon, F.|author3=Lippens, S.|author4=Green, D.R.|author5=Knight, R.|author6=Vandenabeele, P.|author7=Piacentini, M.|author8=Nagata, S.|author9=Borner, C.|author10=Simon, H.U.|author11=Krammer, P.|title=Jürg Tschopp—1951–2011—an immortal contribution|journal=Cell Death and Differentiation|volume=18|year=2011|issue=7|pages=1087–1088|pmc=3131961|doi=10.1038/cdd.2011.46}}</ref> He was the author or co-author of more than 350 publications.<ref name=CellJournal/> He was the co-editor with Gillian M. Griffiths of the 1995 book ''Pathways for Cytolysis''.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Griffiths, Gillian M.|editor2=Tschopp, Jürg|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OVHuCAAAQBAJ|isbn = 9783642794148|title = Pathways for Cytolysis|date = 6 December 2012|publisher = Springer|postscript=; pbk reprint of 1995 hbk 1st edition}}</ref> Tschopp received several awards, including the European Cell Death Organization's Career Award in 2006,<ref>{{cite web|title=ECDO Honorary Awards|website=European Cell Death Organization|url=https://www.ecdo.eu/content/honorary-awards}}</ref> the [[Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]] in 2008,<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Jürg Tschopp. Winner of the 2008 Louis-Jeantet for Medicine|website=Fondation Louis-Jeantet|date=October 2017|url=https://www.jeantet.ch/en/prix-louis-jeantet/laureats/2008-en/professeur-jurg-tschopp/}}</ref> and the [[Novartis Prizes for Immunology#Novartis Prize for Clinical Immunology|Novartis Prize for Clinical Immunology]] (shared with [[Charles Dinarello]]) in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|title=Distinguished Scientific Awards (Novartis Basic and Clinical Immunology Prizes)|website=The American Association of Immunologists|url=https://www.aai.org/About/History/Notable-Members/Distinguished-Scientific-Awards}}</ref>
